solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rock has one sailor landing upside down on another

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down entry, writing the able seaman's letters bottom to top turns them round

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a salt, or old salt, is another word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor capsizes onto a shipmate and hits the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' works because this is a down entry; 'landing' is only a link. AB (able-bodied seaman) and salt are both crossword sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, an example of rock.

clue.text: Supervises as a bishop guilty of pluralism?

definitions.text: as a bishop guilty of pluralism?
definitions.meaning: a pluralist bishop holds more than one diocese, so he is over several sees

explanation.surface: Someone supervises in the manner of a greedy, office-hoarding cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluralism in the church means holding several posts at once; a see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to keep watch over and direct others, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Financial agent supporting manager of museum

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a curator looks after a museum's collection

explanation.surface: A money manager backs the person running a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator is one who manages another's affairs, especially financial ones, as their agent.

clue.text: Man with energy going down gets food

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter for energy drops from the top of the name to the bottom

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fellow with flagging energy grabs something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is a staple grain eaten across the world, an example of food.

clue.text: Every person protecting the Queen must be a multi-talented individual

parts.note: all means everyone
round, as in surrounding, guards what it encloses
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Anyone in the royal protection squad needs to be good at everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every person' gives ALL, and 'protecting' is read as round, meaning surrounding. In cricket an all-rounder both bats and bowls well.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is a person versatile in many skills, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Beastly sounds from areas close to shore?

definitions.meaning: howls of hounds, a dog's baying
inlets of the sea curving into the coast

explanation.surface: Animal noises carry from just off the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds bay, and a bay is a curved stretch of water by the coast.

clue.text: Stream for programme of study

definitions.meaning: a watercourse, the channel a river flows along
a series of lessons, as at college

explanation.surface: Choosing between streams of study at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A river follows its path or channel, and a set of classes is also so named.

clue.text: Climate's bad for one sort of plant

indicators.note: a bad version of the word is a spoilt, jumbled one

explanation.surface: A gardener complains the weather is wrong for a certain plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing garden plant with large flowers, one example of a plant.

clue.text: In grammatical terms, well might that be

definitions.text: In grammatical terms, well might that be

parts.words: In grammatical terms, well might that be
parts.note: the word 'well' modifies verbs, as in 'she sings well', so grammarians class it in a particular way

explanation.surface: A shrug of agreement: grammatically speaking, that may well be so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well might that be' reads as a stock phrase of assent, but 'well' is the word under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as 'well' act as adverbs, so they are described as of that kind in grammar.

clue.text: Possibly an amount to be paid for crossing island

parts.note: the indefinite article

parts.words: amount to be paid for crossing
parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a bridge or road

explanation.surface: Perhaps there is a fee to cross over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island around a lagoon.

clue.text: I, a cruel drunk should show a bit of heart

indicators.note: a drunk set of letters is reeling and disordered

explanation.surface: A boozy brute ought to show a little compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: An auricle is an atrium, an upper chamber of the heart, so part of it.

clue.text: Where speaker maybe given traditional Sunday fare but not a drink

indicators.note: but not signals that the word for a single item is dropped from the meal

parts.note: the Sunday roast is a traditional British meal
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A guest speaker gets the Sunday roast but goes without alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes A from ROAST to leave ROST. A Sunday roast is a traditional British family lunch of roast meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which an orator addresses an audience.

clue.text: Dad who'd lament dreadfully having lost wife

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the remaining letters are badly mangled
having lost means one piece is removed from the words

explanation.surface: A widowed father grieves terribly after losing his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes W out of WHODLAMENT, and 'dreadfully' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The old man is informal slang for one's father.

clue.text: Current time organised for bringing people on board

indicators.note: organised letters have been put into a new order

explanation.surface: Now is the planned time to take on new staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruitment is the process of hiring new members or employees for an organisation.

clue.text: Online help for one wanting to dry out?

definitions.text: Online help for one wanting to dry out?

parts.words: Online help for one wanting to dry out?
parts.note: online is read literally as on a line: a laundry clip helps damp washing hang there to dry, not a recovering drinker

explanation.surface: An internet support service for someone trying to give up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' suggests the internet and 'dry out' suggests sobering up; both are literal laundry here.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing pegged on a line dries out, and the clip holds it there.

clue.text: Offer head affection

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as with a bid
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone shows fondness by offering their head, maybe for a pat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentle warmth and fondness, a synonym of affection.

clue.text: Exist in a state of readiness for plague

parts.note: to be is to exist
set as in ready, set, go

explanation.surface: A community stays prepared for an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to trouble persistently or harass, as a plague does.

clue.text: Dry friend showing lack of humanity

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend with a dry manner comes across as inhuman.
explanation.definitionFit: To act brutally is to behave savagely or cruelly, without compassion.

clue.text: See 13
Little fellow's showing signs of careless shaving?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Nick, a short form of the man's name Nicholas
small cuts made by a razor

explanation.surface: A boy's face shows he was rushed with the razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of Nicholas with a possessive, and small razor cuts, share these letters.

clue.text: Mammal having trouble climbing shrub

parts.note: a camel is a mammal

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A camel struggles to get up a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is an evergreen flowering bush, an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Bill inadequate when this happens in business?

definitions.text: Bill inadequate when this happens in business?

parts.words: Bill inadequate when this happens in business?
parts.note: a business left under the charge of a poor manager is badly run, and an invoice set too low is also described this way

explanation.surface: A firm's invoices fall short when something goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNDER CHARGE, the business is in someone's care; whole, it is billing too little.
explanation.definitionFit: To undercharge is to ask too low a price for goods or services.

clue.text: End of year needs a very strong drink

parts.note: Dec, December, is the year's last month
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: New Year's Eve calls for a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a strong drink; the answer is the opposite, coffee without caffeine.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaff is decaffeinated coffee, a hot drink.

clue.text: See 13
Not at all prudent, following a word of rejection

indicators.note: the word for prudent comes after the word of rejection

parts.note: no is a refusal
wise means sensible or prudent

explanation.surface: Saying no first is anything but sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowise is an archaic adverb meaning in no way, in no manner whatever.

clue.text: Address bill with added expenses

indicators.note: with added signals the expenses join on after the bill

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
costs are expenses

explanation.surface: A firm sends an invoice with extra charges tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them, so to address them.

clue.text: Part of Scotland in risky endeavour

indicators.note: in means the island's name sits within the words risky endeavour

explanation.surface: A Highland adventure that is rather dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides, belonging to Scotland.

clue.text: Town gets modest victories to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the victories ahead of the word for modest

parts.note: wins are victories
low means humble or modest

explanation.surface: A town enjoys some small triumphs early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Winslow is a market town in Buckinghamshire, England, an example of a town.

clue.text: Water's beginning to flow back for swimmer

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word water

parts.note: the tide ebbs when it flows back out to sea

explanation.surface: The sea starts to recede for someone out swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person to swim the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Webb is famous as a pioneering long-distance swimmer.

clue.text: See our paper with yen to be illustrious

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
FT, the Financial Times, is the paper this puzzle appears in
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Look at the Financial Times with its yen for grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means exalted or noble in rank, close to illustrious.

clue.text: More than one diplomat's building seems to be troubled with bias

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomatic missions appear to be plagued by prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the official building of an ambassador, so several are embassies.
